title: One harmonious deformation accounts for all skull differences among crocodilians

fields.label: Label
fields.value: One harmonious deformation accounts for all skull differences among crocodilians

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: Across most crocodilian genera, the skull contours and even the shapes and sizes of individual bones and vacuities can be derived from one another by a single simple coordinate transformation, so that the skull of Notosuchus can be reconstructed bone for bone from that of Crocodilus.

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Ch. XVII: On the Theory of Transformations, or the Comparison of Related Forms

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: To all intents and purposes, then, this not very complex system, representing one harmonious “deformation,” accounts for _all_ the differences between the two figures, and is sufficient to enable one at any time to reconstruct a detailed drawing, bone for bone, of the skull of _Notosuchus_ from the model furnished by the common crocodile.

fields.label: Agent
fields.value: delphisci On Growth and Form claim extractor

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: D’Arcy Wentworth Thompson, On Growth and Form (1st ed., Cambridge: Cambridge University Press, 1917), Chapter XVII, “On the Theory of Transformations, or the Comparison of Related Forms”; topic “Crocodilian and reptile skulls”. Scope: skulls of crocodilians, living and fossil (excluding the oldest forms such as Belodon)

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on thompson1917-ch17-12: resolvable-now, resolvability 0.81

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The reconstruction statement supplies a strong quantitative criterion, and open 3D material spans living and fossil crocodilians. Annotation is substantial but feasible, and residuals can decisively assess whether one transformation accounts for the differences.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Apply one smooth coordinate transformation between homologous crocodilian skull surfaces, sutures and openings, and quantify bone-by-bone reconstruction error against flexible or modular alternatives.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Fossil distortion and missing regions affect fit.

Sutures and vacuities require detailed annotation.

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Living crocodilian skulls are available as CT, so a single-map model can be tested against mosaic change in snout, vault and vacuities. The stronger claim, that Notosuchus can be rebuilt bone for bone from Crocodylus, depends on fossil specimens whose open 3D coverage is thinner and whose distortion is a serious confound. Existing data can settle much of the living comparison and only part of the fossil reconstruction.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Landmark crocodilian skulls, including individual bones and vacuities, fit one simple coordinate map from Crocodylus to other genera, and test whether the map reconstructs Notosuchus bone for bone on held-out landmarks. Support would be low error across most genera; large residuals in particular bones or in Notosuchus would refute the single-deformation account.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Open scans cover living crocodilians more densely than the fossil genera needed for a bone-for-bone reconstruction of Notosuchus.

Fossil crushing mimics coordinate deformation.
